components.name: Windows action
components.description: Browser-native illustration of the standard WinForms action. Native Windows chrome is authoritative.
components.html: <button class="ds-win-action">Start connecting</button><button class="ds-win-action" disabled>Show position arrows</button>
components.css: .ds-win-action { font: 10pt "Segoe UI", sans-serif; min-width:160px; min-height:42px; margin-right:6px; } .ds-win-action:hover:enabled { cursor:default; } .ds-win-action:focus-visible { outline:auto; } .ds-win-action:active:enabled { border-style:inset; }

components.name: Windows text input
components.description: Illustrative native text field from Advanced. Platform controls own border and focus appearance.
components.html: <input class="ds-win-input" aria-label="Wi-Fi fallback" placeholder="Automatic discovery (or iPad IP address)">
components.css: .ds-win-input { font:10pt "Segoe UI", sans-serif; width:100%; min-height:42px; } .ds-win-input:hover { cursor:text; } .ds-win-input:focus-visible { outline:auto; }

components.name: Advanced disclosure link
components.description: A plain link reveals the optional settings area; this preview does not simulate the panel.
components.css: .ds-win-link { font:10pt "Segoe UI", sans-serif; color:#1450aa; text-decoration:underline; } .ds-win-link:hover { cursor:pointer; } .ds-win-link:focus-visible { outline:auto; } .ds-win-link:active { color:LinkText; }

components.name: Windows position arrow
components.description: Illustration of the noninteractive edge overlay. The example points right; source rotates it for the actual edge.
components.html: iPad this way
components.css: .ds-win-arrow { width:152px; height:92px; border-radius:18px; background:#145dd7; color:white; display:flex; flex-direction:column; align-items:center; pointer-events:none; } .ds-win-arrow span { margin-top:4px; font:menu; }

components.name: iPad connection capsule
components.description: Illustrative translation of SwiftUI regularMaterial and Capsule. Material, symbols, and font metrics remain system-rendered in the app.
components.html: PC · USB
components.css: .ds-ipad-capsule { display:inline-flex; align-items:center; gap:12px; padding:10px 16px; border-radius:999px; background:color-mix(in srgb, Canvas 85%, transparent); backdrop-filter:blur(16px); color:CanvasText; font:500 15px system-ui; } .ds-ipad-menu { display:flex; padding:0; border:0; background:transparent; color:LinkText; } .ds-ipad-menu:hover { cursor:pointer; } .ds-ipad-menu:focus-visible { outline:auto; } .ds-ipad-menu:active { opacity:.7; }

narrative.overview:
The platform is the visual authority. Windows uses standard WinForms controls on a restrained light surface; iPad uses SwiftUI system views, symbols, forms, sheets, and materials. Familiar Duet-like utility behavior is the user's direction. There is no custom brand system to extend.

Keep the working display clear. Pairing and connection state receive attention while disconnected; video fills the iPad when available. Position arrows are temporary spatial indicators, separate from connection controls.
keyCharacteristics: Clear connection state with optional settings disclosed separately.
Full-screen video with temporary, unobtrusive overlays.

rules.name: The Platform Color Rule
rules.body: Fixed Windows colors belong to the host; iPad semantic colors and materials remain platform-resolved.

dos: Do use native controls and semantic iPad styling for new surfaces.
Do preserve the distinction between connection state and pairing feedback.
Do keep optional connection configuration under Advanced on Windows.
Do keep position arrows temporary, directional, and separate from menus.
Do preserve native focus, disabled states, Dynamic Type, and Reduce Motion behavior.
donts: Don't add custom branding, decorative dashboards, or persistent chrome over the video.
Don't turn a position arrow into a controls drawer.
Don't treat source behavior, preview captures, or targets as verified live connection or performance results.
